messages:
emma: Heads-up — onboarding call with Acadia Health went well. They want a Redwood Dedicated commit for inference (chat + summarization). Need sizing guidance; they provided expected daily tokens and peak patterns.

raj: share what they gave. we should also flag region constraints (APAC only).

emma: From their telemetry: ~1.2M tokens/day average, 95th day 1.9M. Typical request sizes: median ~120 tokens, p95 ~480 tokens. Traffic shape: strong APAC evening peak (22:00 JST) -> sustained 220 RPS for short 30–45min burst, baseline ~35 RPS.

oliver: sale note — they require 99.9% committed throughput and on-call support window. also asked about canary fallback to hosted for rare spikes.

raj: quick back-of-envelope: target sustained throughput for commit = baseline + headroom for p95 bursts. If we aim for 99th perc SL, plan for ~300 RPS sustained in region. Need to convert RPS -> tokens/sec using avg tokens per request.

taylor: can we run the conversion here? assume avg tokens 200 for safety (between median and p95). 300 RPS * 200 tokens = 60k tokens/sec sustained.

raj: gpu throughput depends on model variant+quant. For our H100-backed config with quantization profile Q4x, we see ~12k tokens/sec per GPU for 2048 context on this workload (empirical). So 60k / 12k = 5 GPUs.

raj: include safety buffer (autoscale cold-start and regional failover). i'd add 20% buffer -> 6 GPUs. recommend committing 6 GPUs in APAC region.

emma: what about burst windows? they want 220 RPS short bursts which at 200 tokens = 44k tokens/sec additional on top of baseline. do we need burst pool?

taylor: if baseline commit handles 60k tokens/sec, short bursts up to +44k would push to ~104k. We support burst with dedicated burst capacity or cross-region spill. Two choices: commit extra 4 GPUs as burst-capable (pay for reserved) or allow hosted fallback (pay-as-you-go) with throttles.

oliver: customer likely wants predictable pricing, they prefer reserved burst rather than opaque hosted billing. they asked for committed throughput guarantee for peak windows.

raj: cost tradeoff: committed vs hosted. rough numbers (cloud + infra amortized): reserved H100-equivalent GPU cost per month ~ $25k. hosted equivalent on-demand bill for spikes varies. If we commit 6 cores (baseline) + 4 burst gpus = 10 GPUs -> ~ $250k/mo._commit pricing can include lower unit price for burst slice.

emma: can we show a small calc snippet for the runbook?

raj: ```
# sizing calc (simplified)
avg_tokens_per_req = 200
planned_rps = 300
required_tokens_per_sec = avg_tokens_per_req * planned_rps  # 60k t/s
per_gpu_tps = 12000  # empirical for H100+Q4x on our model family
gpus_needed = ceil(required_tokens_per_sec / per_gpu_tps)  # 5 -> add buffer -> 6
# burst plan: short extra 44k t/s -> extra_gpus = ceil(44000 / per_gpu_tps) -> 4
```

oliver: looks reasonable. What about p99 latency constraints? they want p99 < 300ms for 512-token requests. Do we have benchmarks?

raj: for 512-token p99 on H100 with batch size tuning we hit ~220-280ms usually. but that's for isolated load. at mixed load we should test. recommend a 2-week soak on dedicated pool with canary traffic mirror.

emma: any region constraints to note? customer data must remain in APAC (no cross-region KV cache). that complicates fallback to hosted (hosted would need APAC capacity or customer consent).

raj: right — fallback must be APAC-hosted or not used. we can allocate burst GPUs in the same region to meet compliance.

sre-oncall: flagging operational limits: we need to reserve capacity in cluster autoscaler to prevent eviction from other tenants. update ResourceQuotas and nodepool labels. Also add runbook step: if disk pressure triggers node replacements during peak deploys -> escalate to infra.

deploy-bot: deployment scheduled: reserved-pool/provisioning-job started for proposal id AC-2026-09 at 1797004534. logs: https://internal.redwood/provision/AC-2026-09

emma: next steps: raj/taylor to validate per_gpu_tps number against current kernel builds (latest perf knobs changed Q4x kernel). run a perf test with 6 GPUs + synthetic burst to confirm p99 latency. oliver to confirm customer's willingness to pay burst reservation vs hosted fallback. i'll draft a short proposal for sales with both options.

taylor: ack. i'll queue the perf runs. aiming for results by EOD tomorrow.

oliver: i'll loop in procurement with a rough budget. thanks all :thumbsup:

raj: one more thing — watch billing anomalies: last month we had cross-zone egress during failover causing unexpected cloud egress. add egress budget line item and make fallback gated by egress threshold.

emma: noted. adding that to proposal.
